shorts.title: The Largest Spider Fossil Ever Found Wasn't a Spider
shorts.hook: In 1980, a fossil was announced as the largest spider ever.
shorts.outro: Doug never let go of the glass. Where the river took him is in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHERE DID THE RIVER TAKE DOUG?
shorts.description: Megarachne was billed as the biggest spider ever until it turned out to be a fifty-four-centimeter freshwater sea scorpion, and the full episode shows where it dragged Doug and his drinking glass.

shorts.title: A Fallen Cliff Revealed a Millipede as Big as a Car
shorts.outro: Doug brought it a saddle made out of a fern, because he wanted to ride it. Full video below.
shorts.description: A sandstone block that fell onto an English beach in 2018 held a piece of Arthropleura, the largest land bug that ever lived, and the full episode reveals whether Doug ever got to ride one.

shorts.title: Six Meters of Sea Scorpion Footprints Were Found on Land
shorts.hook: Someone found six meters of sea scorpion footprints. On land.
shorts.outro: Doug lay down inside its trackway to measure it. It was still walking. Full video below.
shorts.description: A bathtub-sized sea scorpion called Hibbertopterus left a trackway proving it walked out of the water, and the full episode shows what happened when Doug lay down in its path.

shorts.title: This Giant Dragonfly Ruled a Sky With No Birds in It
shorts.hook: Meganeura had a seventy-centimeter wingspan and a sky with no birds.
shorts.outro: It let go at the top of a scale tree. Doug does not have wings. Full video below.
shorts.description: Meganeura hunted in a sky with no birds, bats or pterosaurs to hunt it back, and the full episode reveals how far Doug fell from the top of a scale tree.
